name: Piri Piri Chicken
summary: A whole spatchcocked chicken, slowly basted on the BBQ with a garlicky piri piri sauce. Patience required. Worth it.

steps.instruction: In a pot, melt the butter. Add oil, garlic, bacon, piri piri sauce, oregano, and paprika. Cook over medium heat to develop the sauce.
Spatchcock the chicken: cut along both sides of the backbone and remove it, then flatten the bird. Pierce all over with a knife. Season generously with salt.
Preheat the BBQ. Place chicken skin-side down over indirect heat for 20 minutes.
Flip skin-side up. Spoon sauce slowly over the chicken. Cook 20 minutes. Flip and cook 20 more minutes. Flip one final time and cook another 20 minutes, basting throughout.

name: Pork Souvlaki
summary: Marinated pork tenderloin on skewers, grilled hot and fast. Lemon wedge non-negotiable.

steps.instruction: Cut pork tenderloin into 1-inch cubes.
Combine vinegar, olive oil, garlic, mustard, oregano, paprika, salt, and pepper to make the marinade. Toss pork in marinade and refrigerate at least 2 hours.
Remove from fridge 30 minutes before cooking. Thread pork and chunks of red onion onto skewers.
Grill on a hot BBQ for 4 minutes per side. Rest covered for 5 minutes. Serve with a lemon wedge.

name: Antipasto Salad
summary: Grilled halloumi, hearts of palm, olives, and a punchy red wine vinaigrette. Looks like effort. Takes 20 minutes.

steps.instruction: Slice and prepare all salad vegetables.
Grill halloumi in a dry pan with dried oregano until golden on both sides.
Whisk together red wine vinegar, oil, Dijon, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Arrange everything on a platter or toss in a bowl. Drizzle with dressing and serve immediately.

name: Love Salad
summary: A Ricardo rice salad with ginger-soy dressing, cashews, spinach, and raisins. The kind of salad people ask for the recipe of.

steps.instruction: In a small saucepan, cook the garlic and ginger in 2 tbsp of the oil until golden. Transfer to a bowl, discard the ginger. Add remaining oil, soy sauce, and honey. Mix well.
In a large bowl, combine all salad ingredients.
Pour dressing over the salad. Season with pepper. Toss and serve immediately.

name: Italian Pasta Salad
summary: Penne, salami, cherry tomatoes, and a maple-dijon vinaigrette. The lunchbox pasta salad that holds up by Thursday.

steps.instruction: Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain, rinse with cold water, drain again.
Whisk together oil, red wine vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon, and Italian seasoning in a large bowl.
Add pasta, lettuce, salami, tomatoes, and onion to the bowl. Toss well to combine.

name: Quick Pickles
summary: Lebanese cucumbers in a honey-vinegar brine. Ready after a few hours in the fridge. Katerine's recipe.

steps.instruction: Mix water, vinegar, and honey until honey dissolves.
Add the sliced cucumbers. Refrigerate for a few hours before serving.

name: Fried Pork and Cilantro Meatballs
summary: Ground pork meatballs packed with fresh cilantro, pan-fried until golden. Simple, fragrant, satisfying.

steps.instruction: Combine pork, cilantro, garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, egg, and breadcrumbs. Mix well. Form into golf ball-sized meatballs.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry meatballs in batches, turning occasionally, for 10–12 minutes until cooked through and golden on all sides.
Drain on paper towels. Serve with rice or noodles.

name: Burrito Bowl
summary: Spiced ground beef over rice with black beans, corn, and all the toppings. Weeknight dinner at full volume.

steps.instruction: Brown the ground beef and onion in a skillet over medium-high heat. Drain excess fat.
Season with chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Stir in salsa. Simmer 5 minutes.
Build bowls: rice, then beef mixture, then black beans and corn. Top with cheese, sour cream, avocado, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

name: BBQ Pork Ribs
summary: Dry-rubbed ribs slow-cooked in the oven, then finished on the BBQ with a sticky homemade sauce. A weekend project with a clear reward.

steps.instruction: Remove the membrane from the back of the ribs. Mix brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, dry mustard, cayenne, and salt into a dry rub. Coat ribs generously on all sides.
Wrap ribs tightly in foil. Bake at 275°F for 2.5–3 hours until tender.
While ribs bake, combine ketchup, apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire, honey, and hot sauce in a small saucepan. Simmer 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Unwrap ribs and brush generously with sauce. Grill over medium heat for 10–15 minutes, turning and basting until caramelized.

name: Tuna Bread Cups
summary: Sliced bread pressed into muffin tins, filled with a creamy tuna mixture, and baked until crispy. A retro classic that still works.

steps.instruction: Preheat oven to 375°F. Flatten each bread slice with a rolling pin. Press into greased muffin tin cups to form little bread bowls.
Mix tuna, mayo, celery, onion, mustard, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Fill each bread cup with tuna mixture. Top with shredded cheese.
Bake 15–18 minutes until edges are golden and cheese is melted.

name: Deep-Dish Pizza
summary: Thick, focaccia-style crust topped with chunky tomato sauce, sausage, and a lot of cheese. Chicago by way of the family kitchen.

steps.instruction: Oil a 9×13" baking pan generously. Press dough into the pan and up the sides to form a thick crust. Let rest 15 minutes.
Brown the sausage in a skillet, breaking it apart. Drain. Add garlic, crushed tomatoes, oregano, basil, and red pepper flakes. Simmer 10 minutes.
Spread mozzarella over the dough. Top with sausage sauce. Sprinkle Parmesan over everything.
Bake at 425°F for 25–30 minutes until crust is golden and cheese is bubbling.

name: Al Pastor Pork
summary: Pork shoulder marinated in chili, achiote, and pineapple, then roasted or grilled. Tacos optional but strongly encouraged.

steps.instruction: Blend soaked chilies, achiote, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, oregano, and cumin until smooth.
Toss pork slices in the marinade. Refrigerate at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Grill or roast pork at 400°F for 20–25 minutes until charred at the edges. Add pineapple chunks in the last 5 minutes.
Chop meat and serve in warm tortillas with diced onion, cilantro, and pineapple.

name: Lemon Chicken
summary: Chicken thighs braised in a bright lemon-herb sauce. Straightforward enough for Tuesday, good enough for company.

steps.instruction: Season chicken with salt and pepper. Sear in olive oil over medium-high heat, skin-side down, for 5 minutes until golden. Flip and cook 3 more minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add garlic and cook 1 minute. Add lemon juice, zest, broth, thyme, rosemary, and honey. Stir.
Return chicken to the pan, skin-side up. Simmer over medium-low heat, covered, for 20–25 minutes until cooked through. Spoon sauce over before serving.

name: Pad Thai
summary: Rice noodles, shrimp, eggs, and bean sprouts in a tamarind-fish sauce. Real pad thai flavour, made at home.

steps.instruction: Soak rice noodles in warm water for 30 minutes. Drain. Mix tamarind, fish sauce, and sugar in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry shrimp until pink. Push to the side, scramble the eggs in the centre.
Add noodles and garlic. Pour sauce over. Toss everything together for 2–3 minutes until noodles absorb the sauce.
Add bean sprouts and green onions. Toss briefly. Serve topped with crushed peanuts and a lime wedge.

name: Pizza Dough
summary: A reliable yeast dough that works for thin crust, deep dish, or anywhere in between. Makes enough for two pies.

steps.instruction: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water. Let sit 5–10 minutes until foamy.
Stir in olive oil and salt. Add flour one cup at a time, mixing until a shaggy dough forms. Turn onto a floured surface and knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled.
Punch down the dough. Divide into two portions. Use immediately or wrap and refrigerate for up to 2 days.

name: Pâté Chinois
summary: Quebec's answer to shepherd's pie. Ground beef and creamed corn under a layer of mashed potatoes. Golden on top. Comfort in a pan.

steps.instruction: Boil potatoes until tender. Drain and mash with butter, warm milk, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Brown ground beef and onion in a skillet. Season with salt and pepper. Drain excess fat.
Spread beef mixture in a greased 9×13" baking dish. Layer creamed corn and whole kernel corn over the beef. Spread mashed potatoes evenly on top.
Bake at 375°F for 20–25 minutes until the potato top is lightly golden. Broil the last 2 minutes for extra colour.

name: Laotian Grilled Chicken
summary: Chicken marinated in lemongrass, fish sauce, and galangal, then grilled over charcoal. The marinade does the work.

steps.instruction: Blend or mince lemongrass, galangal, and garlic together. Mix with fish sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and sesame oil to make the marinade.
Score the chicken pieces deeply so the marinade penetrates. Coat thoroughly and marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Grill over medium heat, turning frequently, for 35–40 minutes until cooked through with charred edges. Baste with leftover marinade as it cooks.
Rest 5 minutes. Serve with steamed rice and cilantro.

name: Poke Bowl
summary: Ahi tuna marinated in soy and sesame, served over rice with avocado, edamame, and pickled cucumber. Better than the one at the mall.

steps.instruction: Toss diced tuna with soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and sriracha. Let marinate 10 minutes.
Divide warm rice between two bowls.
Arrange tuna, avocado, edamame, and cucumber over the rice. Top with green onions, sesame seeds, and a drizzle of remaining marinade.

name: Miso Ginger Chicken
summary: Chicken thighs glazed in white miso, ginger, and honey, roasted until caramelised. Goes with rice, noodles, or just as is.

steps.instruction: Whisk miso, ginger, garlic, honey, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame oil together. Reserve 2 tbsp of marinade for glazing. Coat chicken in the rest and marinate 30 minutes or overnight.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Arrange chicken in a single layer in a baking dish.
Roast 25–30 minutes, brushing with reserved glaze halfway through, until caramelised and cooked through. Top with sesame seeds and green onions.

name: Chicken Satay
summary: Lemongrass-marinated chicken skewers served with a rich peanut dipping sauce. The sauce is the point.

steps.instruction: Mix lemongrass, fish sauce, turmeric, and sugar. Toss chicken strips in the marinade and thread onto skewers. Marinate at least 30 minutes.
Whisk peanut butter, coconut milk, soy sauce, lime juice, garlic, and sriracha together for the dipping sauce. Warm gently if needed.
Grill skewers over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side until cooked through and lightly charred. Serve with peanut sauce.

name: Chicken Rice-a-Roni
summary: Chicken thighs over broken spaghetti and rice, all cooked together in seasoned broth until golden and fluffy. A one-pot weeknight staple.

steps.instruction: Season chicken with paprika, salt, and pepper. Sear in butter and oil over medium-high heat, 4 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, toast broken spaghetti pieces and rice until golden, about 3 minutes. Add onion and garlic, cook 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth and thyme. Nestle chicken thighs on top. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 20 minutes until rice is tender and chicken is cooked through.
Rest covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork, top with parsley, and serve.

name: Rocky Road
summary: Melted dark chocolate with marshmallows, nuts, and whatever else you want to throw in. Refrigerate and cut into squares.

steps.instruction: Melt chocolate chips, butter, and condensed milk together in a double boiler or microwave in 30-second intervals, stirring until smooth.
Remove from heat. Fold in marshmallows and nuts.
Spread into a parchment-lined 8×8" pan. Refrigerate at least 2 hours until firm. Cut into squares.

name: St-Hubert Style Coleslaw
summary: A creamy, lightly sweet coleslaw that tastes suspiciously close to the one from the chicken chain. Paired with anything off the grill.

steps.instruction: Combine shredded cabbage and grated carrot in a large bowl.
Whisk together mayo, vinegar, sugar, celery salt, and onion powder until smooth.
Pour dressing over the slaw and toss well. Refrigerate at least 30 minutes before serving for the flavours to meld.

name: Corn and Blueberry Salad
summary: Grilled corn, fresh blueberries, red onion, and feta in a honey-lime dressing. A summer salad that genuinely surprises people.

steps.instruction: Grill or roast corn. Cut kernels off the cob.
Combine corn, blueberries, red onion, feta, and cilantro in a bowl.
Whisk lime juice, honey, and olive oil together. Pour over salad. Toss and serve at room temperature or chilled.

name: Udon Miso Chicken Salad
summary: Chewy udon noodles with shredded chicken, red cabbage, and edamame in a white miso dressing. Cold, satisfying, and better the next day.

steps.instruction: Whisk miso, rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and honey until smooth.
Combine cooled noodles, shredded chicken, cabbage, edamame, carrot, and green onions in a large bowl.
Pour dressing over and toss to coat. Top with sesame seeds. Serve cold.

name: Ham and Pasta Salad
summary: Rotini with diced ham, cheese cubes, and vegetables in a creamy dressing. The pasta salad that shows up at every gathering and disappears first.

steps.instruction: Cook pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk together mayo, sour cream, vinegar, dill, salt, and pepper.
Combine pasta with ham, cheese, vegetables, and dressing. Toss well. Refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.

name: Laotian Larb
summary: Minced pork with toasted rice powder, fish sauce, lime, and loads of fresh herbs. One of those dishes that tastes completely alive.

steps.instruction: Toast uncooked rice in a dry pan over medium heat, shaking constantly, until golden and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Grind in a mortar or spice grinder to a coarse powder.
Cook ground pork in a dry pan over medium-high heat, breaking it apart, until just cooked through. Remove from heat.
Toss warm pork with fish sauce, lime juice, shallots, chili, and sugar. Let stand 2 minutes.
Add mint, cilantro, and green onions. Sprinkle toasted rice powder over top. Toss gently and serve immediately with sticky rice.

name: Vietnamese Salad
summary: Rice noodles, shredded chicken, cucumber, and herbs in a classic nuoc cham dressing. Fresh, bright, and ready in 20 minutes.

steps.instruction: Whisk fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, garlic, and chili together to make the dressing. Taste and adjust balance.
Combine noodles, chicken, cucumber, carrot, bean sprouts, mint, and cilantro in a large bowl.
Pour dressing over and toss well. Top with crushed peanuts and serve immediately.

name: Mediterranean Grilled Salmon
summary: Salmon fillets marinated in lemon, olive oil, garlic, and herbs, then grilled quickly. Dinner in under 30 minutes.

steps.instruction: Mix olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, thyme, paprika, and salt. Coat salmon fillets and marinate 15 minutes.
Grill over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side, or until the fish flakes easily.
Serve topped with capers and fresh parsley.

name: Grilled Salmon with Peanut Ginger Sauce
summary: Salmon grilled with a soy glaze, served over a warm peanut-ginger sauce. An Asian-inspired riff that earns its place in the rotation.

steps.instruction: Mix soy sauce, honey, and sesame oil. Brush over salmon fillets.
Whisk together peanut butter, ginger, garlic, lime juice, coconut milk, and sriracha until smooth. Warm gently in a small saucepan.
Grill salmon over medium-high heat, 4 minutes per side until cooked through.
Spoon peanut ginger sauce over each fillet. Top with green onions and serve.

name: Pork Skewers with Yogurt and Tomato Sauce
summary: Grilled pork skewers slid over pita soaked in hot beef stock, then yogurt and tomato sauce on top. Part kebab, part soup, fully Greek.

ingredients.name: strained plain or thick Greek yogurt

steps.instruction: Thread the pork cubes onto 8 wooden skewers and set them on a platter. Sprinkle with oregano, season with pepper, and brush with olive oil. Cover and refrigerate until needed.
Make the tomato sauce: melt 3 tbsp butter in a pan. Add the garlic and cook over low heat, stirring often, for 1–2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, and a pinch of cayenne. Season with pepper and simmer 5–10 minutes until thickened. Let cool, then chill.
An hour before serving, preheat the broiler or light the barbecue. Brush both sides of the pitas with the 5 tbsp melted butter and broil or grill for a couple of minutes. Keep warm.
Cook the skewers under the broiler or over charcoal for 10–15 minutes until cooked through, brushing with oil and turning often.
Meanwhile, heat the beef stock and the tomato sauce in separate pans. Cut the pitas into pieces and divide among individual soup plates.

Spoon 5–6 tbsp hot beef stock into each plate and spread 2–3 tbsp yogurt on top. Slide the meat off 2 skewers onto each plate and spoon 3–4 tbsp tomato sauce over it. Sprinkle with pepper and cayenne. Serve immediately.

name: Chicken Shawarma
summary: Sliced chicken breast marinated an hour in seven spices and lemon, pan-cooked, then rolled in warm flatbread with hummus and a crisp parsley-cilantro salad.

steps.instruction: Put the chicken, garlic, olive oil, seven spices seasoning, 1 teaspoon pepper, sea salt, chili flakes, and lemon juice into a bowl, mix well, and let marinate for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, put the lettuce, parsley, cilantro (coriander), and tomatoes in another bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Heat a large skillet or frying pan, add all the chicken and marinade, and cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, for 10-15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice and remove the pan from the heat.
Lay out the warm flatbreads and divide the salad between them. Spoon the chicken on top, add a spoonful of hummus to each, and roll up tightly. Serve immediately.

name: Napa Cabbage & Leek Spicy Chicken Rice Porridge
summary: A one-pot spicy rice porridge from napa cabbage, leeks and shredded chicken, built to use whatever vegetables are on hand.

ingredients.name: leeks, white and light green parts, sliced

steps.instruction: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the leeks for 3 minutes until soft, then stir in the gochujang and pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the water, chicken broth powder, rice and whole chicken breast. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then so the rice doesn't stick.
Lift the chicken out, shred it with two forks, and return it to the pot.
Add the napa cabbage and cook for about 8 minutes, until the cabbage is soft and the rice has broken down into a porridge. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Taste and add more gochujang, pepper flakes or broth powder if needed.

name: Chinese Smashed Cucumber Salad
summary: Smashed cucumber in a sharp soy, rice vinegar and sesame dressing. Cold, crunchy, and built to sit next to something rich like char siu.

ingredients.name: chili flakes or chili oil, optional

steps.instruction: Smash the cucumbers with the flat of a knife, then cut them into bite-size chunks.
Toss with the salt and let sit 10 minutes. Drain off the water.
Whisk the rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and garlic. Toss with the cucumber.
Chill 10-15 minutes if you have time. Top with sesame seeds, and chili if using.

name: Nam Khao (Lao Crispy Rice Salad)
summary: Curry-spiced rice balls fried until crunchy, crumbled and tossed with cured pork, herbs and lime, then wrapped in lettuce. Crunchy, sour and salty all at once.

steps.instruction: Cook the rinsed jasmine rice with the water: bring to a boil, drop to low, cover and cook 15 minutes. Spread it on a tray and let it cool for about an hour. Do not refrigerate it.
Whisk the egg with the red curry paste and sugar in a small bowl.
Put the cooled rice in a large bowl. Pour in the curry egg mixture, add the coconut shreds and lime leaves, and mix well.
Pack the rice mixture firmly into handful-sized balls or disks.
Fry the rice balls in oil at 350F for about 10 minutes, until deep golden brown.
Crumble the fried rice balls into a large bowl. Add the fish sauce and lime juice, mix, and season with salt.
Fold in the cured pork, pork skin, cilantro, green onion and peanuts.
Top with fried chili and serve in lettuce leaves as wraps. Best eaten right away.

name: Maple Garlic Roasted Carrots
summary: Oven-roasted carrots glazed with maple syrup and garlic, caramelized at the edges. Built to sit next to BBQ pulled pork.

ingredients.name: smoked paprika or chili flakes, optional
lemon juice or cider vinegar, to finish

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 425F and line a sheet pan. Cut the peeled carrots into sticks or halve them lengthwise, and pat dry.
Toss the carrots with the olive oil, maple syrup, garlic, salt, pepper, and paprika or chili flakes if using.
Spread in a single layer without crowding the pan. Roast 25 to 30 minutes, flipping once halfway, until tender and caramelized at the edges.
If the garlic browns too fast, stir it in for the last 10 minutes instead. Finish with a squeeze of lemon or a splash of cider vinegar.

name: Gwangyang-Style Bulgogi
summary: Unmarinated bulgogi from Gwangyang, seasoned just before grilling so the charcoal and beef do the talking.

ingredients.name: beef sirloin, thinly sliced to 1/8 inch (4 mm) thick
scallion, thinly sliced, or pine nut powder (optional)

steps.instruction: In a large bowl, stir together the soy sauce, brown sugar, wine, garlic, sesame oil, and black pepper. Set aside.
Prepare an outdoor grill (barbecue), preferably charcoal.
Just before grilling, fold the beef into the soy mixture. Add the slices to the grill and cook evenly on both sides.
If desired, garnish the plated meat with thinly sliced scallion or pine nut powder to finish.

name: LA Short Rib Gui (LA Galbi)
summary: Flanken-cut short ribs in a pear-and-soy marinade for 12 hours to a day, then a quick, gentle pan sear (35 minutes active).

steps.instruction: Because the short ribs were cut across a lot of bones, there may be impurities or bone fragments attached to the flesh. Rinse the ribs under cold running water, then set them in a sieve to drain well. Pat dry with paper towels.

Make the marinade: Grate the pear into a bowl. Add 6 tablespoons water, the soy sauce, wine, mirin, corn syrup, brown sugar, garlic, scallion, sesame oil, ginger, and black pepper and stir until well incorporated.
In a large airtight container, combine the short ribs and the marinade and mix until well incorporated. Let marinate for at least 12 hours and up to 1 day in the refrigerator.

To finish: When ready to cook, remove the container from the refrigerator. Place the marinated short ribs in a large, cold frying pan and set the pan over medium-low heat (higher heat will caramelize or burn the marinade). Cook for 2 minutes on each side, or until both sides are well cooked.
Serve the cooked short ribs garnished with the scallion. (Cooking time in the book: 10 to 15 minutes.)

name: Doenjang-Marinated Pork Gui
summary: Thin pork belly coated in doenjang and wine for a deeper, nuttier, more savory sear.
source: Korean cookbook (Doenjang Yangnyeom Dwaeji Gui, 된장양념돼지구이)

ingredients.name: pork belly, thinly sliced to 1/16 inch (2 mm) thick

steps.instruction: In a bowl, stir together the doenjang and wine and have the baster ready.

Heat a frying pan over medium heat. Add the slices of pork to the pan, avoiding overlap. Flip the meat when the first side is cooked. After flipping, brush the meat with the baster. Repeat until all the meat is cooked. Transfer the cooked meat to a plate once cooked.
Serve garnished with sesame seeds, chives, and scallion and serve immediately.

Variation: If you have slices of pork belly thicker than 3/8 inch (1 cm), mix the doenjang and wine in a small bowl. Score the slices of pork belly and cut into 2 1/2-inch (6 cm) lengths if needed. In a large bowl or container, coat the pork with the marinade and cover. Let marinate for a minimum of 1 hour, up to 1 day. Heat a frying pan over medium heat and cook until fully cooked on both sides. Serve garnished with sesame seeds, chives, and scallion.

name: Cucumber Saengchae (Oi-Saengchae)
summary: Salted, rinsed cucumber half-moons tossed in a sharp gochugaru-vinegar sauce; serves 2 to 4.

steps.instruction: In-season farmers' market cucumbers will probably have tiny stiff hairs; use coarse salt or a clean scrub to wipe down any spikes.
Halve the cucumber lengthwise and cut crosswise into 1/4-inch (6 mm) half-moons.

In a bowl, combine the sliced cucumber with the salt and let brine for 10 minutes. After 10 minutes, thoroughly rinse off the salt in cold water. Drain and gently squeeze with your hands to get rid of any excess moisture and set aside.
Make the sauce: Combine all the sauce ingredients into a bowl and mix until well combined. Combine with the cucumbers and mix until evenly seasoned. Plate and serve.

name: Doenjang Napa Cabbage Namul (Doenjang Baechu Namul)
summary: Quick-blanched napa cabbage, iced, squeezed dry and massaged with doenjang, soy sauce and sesame oil; serves 2 to 4.
source: Korean cookbook (Doenjang Baechu Namul, 된장 배추 나물)

steps.instruction: Remove any bruised or discolored leaves from the napa cabbage and cut out the tough root. Separate each leaf and rinse well with cold running water.

Set up a bowl of ice and water. In a large pot, combine 8 1/2 cups (68 fl oz / 2 liters) water and the salt and bring to a boil. Holding all the leaves together, dip the bottom (thicker) halves into the boiling water and blanch for 30 seconds. Drop the leaves in and blanch for another 30 seconds, a total of 1 minute. Immediately remove and transfer to the ice bath (or under cold running water) to stop further cooking.

Once fully cooled, remove the leaves and gently squeeze with your hands to remove all water. Cut the drained leaves into 2-inch (5 cm) lengths and tear with your hands along the grain of the cabbage into bite-size pieces.
In a bowl, combine the doenjang, soy sauce, and sesame oil and mix until fully combined. Add the shredded cabbage pieces and massage to marinate until well combined.
Serve garnished with the sliced scallion, if desired.

name: Bean Sprout Namul (Kongnamul)
summary: Soybean sprouts boiled 2 minutes and tossed in garlic, scallion and sesame oil, with spicy, tangy and mung bean variations; serves 2 to 4.

steps.instruction: Remove any bruised or dirty parts of the bean sprouts, including all the stringy roots, with your hands or scissors. Quickly rinse the sprouts in cold water and transfer to a sieve. The bean sprouts will easily start to go bad after washing, so it's best to use them as soon as possible.

In a large pot, combine 8 1/2 cups (68 fl oz / 2 liters) water and the salt and bring to a boil. Add the bean sprouts, return to a boil, and boil for 2 minutes. Scoop the bean sprouts out of the water with a sieve and let cool to room temperature.
Make the sauce: In a large bowl, mix together the garlic, scallion, soy sauce, salt, and sesame oil.
Fold the bean sprouts into the sauce and lightly toss until evenly coated. Mound the bean sprouts on a flat plate or shallow bowl and garnish with the chili threads and sesame seeds, if desired.
Variation (spicy): add 1 tablespoon gochugaru (red chili flakes) to the sauce.
Variation (refreshing): add 1 tablespoon rice vinegar and 1 teaspoon sugar to the sauce.

Variation (Mung Bean Sprout Namul): make this with mung bean sprouts instead of soybean sprouts, reducing the blanching time and making up for the lack of texture by adding blanched minari and julienned mild red peppers.

name: Spinach Namul (Sigeumchi Namul)
summary: Spinach blanched for 20 seconds, iced and dressed in soy sauce, sesame oil and ground sesame seeds; keeps 2 days in the fridge.
source: Korean cookbook (Sigeumchi Namul, 시금치 나물), Banchan chapter, p. 166

steps.instruction: Remove any blemished spinach leaves (and trim off roots if the spinach is from the farmers' market). Separate the leaves and stems. Halve the bottoms of the stems lengthwise and rinse the cut leaves in cold water two or three times until clean, making sure all dirt at the root end of the stems is washed away.

Set up a bowl of ice and water. In a large pot, bring 8 1/2 cups (68 fl oz / 2 liters) water and the salt to a boil. Add the spinach and blanch for 20 seconds. Scoop out immediately and transfer to the ice bath to cool completely. (Cooking time will vary depending on the type of spinach and its toughness, but spinach is easily overcooked and quickly loses its crunchy texture, which is important to this recipe.) Drain well and squeeze to remove excess moisture.
Make the sauce: In a bowl, stir together the soy sauce, salt, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.
Transfer the spinach to the bowl and toss well with the sauce until fully coated. Plate on a shallow bowl or a plate. Kept in an airtight container, this will keep up to 2 days in the refrigerator.
Variation: For a deeper and earthier taste, replace the soy sauce with 1 tablespoon doenjang (fermented soybean paste).

name: Ssamjang (Korean Spicy Dipping Sauce)
summary: Doenjang and gochujang dipping sauce for grilled meat, rice and lettuce wraps; keeps about 10 days chilled, best fresh.

ingredients.name: honey (use less or skip to reduce sweetness)

steps.instruction: Using a spoon, thoroughly mix all the ingredients in a large bowl.
Transfer the mixture to a small bowl and serve with rice and lettuce, or alongside grilled meat. Keeps about 10 days in the refrigerator, though it tastes best freshly made.

name: Korean BBQ Spread
summary: Three grilled meats (Gwangyang bulgogi, LA galbi, doenjang pork) with ssamjang and four cold or blanched sides; start the galbi the night before.
source: Korean cookbook (Gwangyang Bulgogi, LA Galbi, Doenjang Pork Gui, Banchan chapter) and Maangchi (ssamjang)

ingredients.name: BULGOGI: beef sirloin, thinly sliced to 1/8 inch (4 mm) thick
BULGOGI: scallion, thinly sliced, or pine nut powder (optional)
GALBI marinade: jinjang (dark Korean soy sauce)
GALBI marinade: freshly ground black pepper
GALBI: scallion (spring onion), slivered, to finish
PORK GUI: pork belly, thinly sliced to 1/16 inch (2 mm) thick
PORK GUI: small scallion (spring onion), slivered
CUCUMBER SAENGCHAE sauce: fine gochugaru (red chili powder)

steps.instruction: The night before (12 hours up to 1 day ahead): make the galbi. Rinse the short ribs under cold water, drain well and pat dry. Grate the pear into a bowl, add 6 tablespoons water and the rest of the marinade ingredients, stir until incorporated, then mix with the ribs in an airtight container and refrigerate. See the LA Short Rib Gui recipe.
Make the ssamjang: mix all the ssamjang ingredients thoroughly with a spoon and transfer to a small bowl. See the Ssamjang recipe.
Make the cold side: salt the sliced cucumber for 10 minutes, rinse, squeeze, then toss with the sauce (Cucumber Saengchae).

Make the blanched sides, using the same pot of salted water where you can: napa cabbage 1 minute total, spinach 20 seconds, then ice bath; bean sprouts boiled 2 minutes and cooled to room temperature. Squeeze the greens dry and dress each with its sauce (Doenjang Napa Cabbage Namul, Spinach Namul, Bean Sprout Namul).
Prepare an outdoor grill (barbecue), preferably charcoal, or a frying pan. Stir the bulgogi seasoning together and the pork doenjang-and-wine baster.

Grill the bulgogi: just before grilling, fold the sirloin into the soy mixture, add to the grill and cook evenly on both sides. Garnish with scallion or pine nut powder if desired (Gwangyang-Style Bulgogi).

Cook the pork gui: in a frying pan over medium heat, cook the pork belly slices without overlap, flip when the first side is cooked, brush with the doenjang-wine baster, repeat until cooked. Garnish with sesame seeds, chives and scallion (Doenjang-Marinated Pork Gui).

Cook the galbi: place the marinated short ribs in a large, cold frying pan, set over medium-low heat and cook about 2 minutes per side until well cooked. Garnish with slivered scallion (LA Short Rib Gui).
Serve everything together with lettuce, rice, ssamjang and the sides.

name: Gallinas Borrachas (Poulet au vin blanc)
summary: Drunken chicken from Coahuila, simmered with chorizo, ham, white wine, raisins and almonds, with a quiet hit of cinnamon and clove.

ingredients.name: vin blanc sec ou vinaigre de xérès

steps.instruction: Dans le bol d'un mixeur, réduire les tomates en purée.

Dans une sauteuse, chauffer l'huile et ajouter les morceaux de poulet. Ajouter les tomates, l'ail et le persil. Cuire à feu moyen 10 à 15 minutes, en retournant les morceaux de poulet de temps à autre.
Ajouter le chorizo et le jambon et cuire encore 5 minutes. Verser le vin blanc et poursuivre la cuisson pour réduire le jus.

Incorporer le sucre, les clous de girofle, la cannelle, le poivre, la noix muscade, les raisins secs et les amandes. Saler. Réduire le feu et cuire 15 minutes ou jusqu'à ce que le poulet soit bien cuit et le jus suffisamment épais.
Disposer un morceau de poulet sur chaque assiette. Napper de sauce et servir avec du riz ou de la salade.
